text:
Anya: quick sync: operators keep seeing weird oscillations when hedges get tweaked mid-rollout. I think we need a clearer manifest delta model + escrowed apply semantics. Thoughts?
Ravi: yep. My hypothesis: controller pushes small hedge changes and runtimes apply them immediately which causes transient capacity reshuffles. We should support atomic delta commits with an optional grace_window to let in-flight requests finish.
Sam: agree on grace_window. Also propose a signed apply token so runtimes can validate the change origin (HMAC) and avoid partial race applies from lagging controllers.
Tess: Signed token + seq isn't enough for Private installs where controllers are on a different cadence. Can we add a merge strategy: apply if seq > local_seq OR if delta is additive (only loosening hedges)?
Anya: merge strategy makes sense. Let's define three merge modes: strict (reject non-equal seq), additive-only (only increases windows/cost caps), and permissive (last-writer wins). Default to additive-only during canary.
Ravi: example manifest patch flow idea: controller publishes base manifest and diffs. runtimes fetch diffs and compute apply_plan. They then request an apply_token via /apply?plan_id which returns signed token valid for N seconds. If token missing, runtime enters conservative enforcement.
Sam: Also add an emergency_override boolean in manifest to allow ops to force immediate active apply during incidents — but require audit webhook and a short kill-switch TTL so it's not sticky.
Tess: For local heuristics: allow runtime to probe model warmth and request a temporary "probe-hedge" that is explicitly bounded (max_extra_ms, max_cost_delta). Probe requests must include decision_id and sample flag. Controller will sample at 0.5% by default.
Anya: Telemetry: we need fields per sampled decision: decision_id, manifest_seq, probe_result_ms, made_local_decision?, reason_code. These should be batched to telemetry with a per-tenant cap.
Ravi: Ops edge-case: what if a runtime can't reach controller for an apply_token but still has diffs? We should let it operate in a "stale-grace" mode: honor last active manifest for up to N minutes, then revert to conservative defaults. Configurable per-deployment.
Sam: conservative defaults = no cross-tier hedging, single-tier naive retry, cost_cap = min(account_quota, global_guardrail). Spell out the concrete numbers in RFC.
Tess: security note: tokens should be short-lived (30s) and rotated. Use mutual TLS for hosted controller calls; for private we support bearer with key rotation and aud claim.
Anya: sample manifest (json patch style):
```json
{ "base_seq": 101, "patch_id": "p-7a9", "merge_mode": "additive-only", "changes": [ { "tier": "standard", "add_windows_ms": [3] }, { "tier": "premium", "set_cost_cap_cents_per_1k": 45 } ], "grace_window_s": 20, "emergency_override": false }
```
Ravi: CI/Lint: enforce that patches can't exceed tenant_quota and that additive-only patches aren't secretly lowering windows. Add a preflight sim job that runs with a lightweight scheduler to predict likely slot reassignments.
Sam: Implementation plan: 1) manifest delta RFC + merge_mode semantics 2) apply_token endpoint + audit webhook 3) runtime stale-grace mode + backoff timers 4) probe-hedge telemetry and sampled upload 5) canary 2 regions 6) postmortem checklist.
Tess: Minor ops detail: add an operator-visible timeline in Console for manifest changes (who, when, diff, merge_mode, token_issued). Helps debugging when tenants report regressions.
ops-bot: @deploybot scheduled canary for manifest-delta-svc v0.2 to staging cluster B. job=90012.
Anya: I'll draft the RFC with the merge semantics and numeric defaults (stale_grace 5m, token_ttl 30s, probe_sample 0.5%). Please leave comments by EOD Friday.
Ravi: I'll prototype the token endpoint and the signed token format.
Sam: I'll add the preflight sim harness to infra repo.
Tess: I'll own console timeline + ops runbook.
Anya: thanks team — let's keep the delta model tight so we avoid dance-of-death capacity oscillations.
